official.deadline_note: Single central closing date administered through Aurora's Indigenous Pathways Portal; no separate institutional deadline is published. The 2026 round opened 16 June 2026 and closed 11 September 2026; no 2027 window is published as at the verification date.
official.application_cycle: 2026 round (opened 16 June 2026, closed 11 September 2026); Aurora states up to four scholarships will be awarded yearly from 2024 to 2026
official.status_note: Aurora's Indigenous Pathways Portal marks the 2026 round as 'Closed' (Open 16/06/2026, Close 11/09/2026). Aurora states up to four scholarships are awarded yearly from 2024 to 2026 and no 2027 application window is published as at the verification date.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Published list of purposes the scholarship may be used for includes 'University fees/payment of HECS'.
benefits: Up to $120,000 AUD per year, for up to three years, as a contribution towards the cost of full-time postgraduate study or research
Up to $5,000 AUD per year in tailored academic and wellbeing support
Scaffolded personal, social, academic and wellbeing support facilitated by Aurora
Academic and cultural guidance from an Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander individual with postgraduate study and/or research experience
Community and network-building opportunities with fellow scholars and Aurora's Alumni network, including gatherings, networking events and retreats
No need to re-apply each year once awarded
eligibility: Be of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander descent, identify as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander, and be accepted as such by the community in which you live or have lived
Provide written confirmation of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander identity from an incorporated Indigenous organisation or Land Council

Provide written confirmation of full-time enrolment in a postgraduate course (graduate certificate, masters or PhD) at a recognised university in Australia, the US or the UK, OR written confirmation from a recognised research institute
Be undertaking full-time graduate study or research in a cancer-related field in health, research and policy
Provide a budget outlining how the Scholarship funds will be used, including all additional funding and income

Demonstrate how the graduate study or research will impact Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander communities in improving cancer-related outcomes, and an aspiration towards employment or continued employment in a cancer-related field
requirements: Read the Scholarship Guidelines before applying to confirm eligibility criteria and required documents

Submit an application with all required documents by the Scholarship closing date; Aurora states the application will not be considered complete or pass the shortlisting process if all required documents are not submitted by the closing date
All references must be emailed by the referee directly to scholarships@aurorafoundation.com.au
Scholarship funds cannot be used for study or research-related expenses that should be covered by the university or institute
documents: Personal statement of no more than two pages covering community identification and contributions, the course or research focus areas, impact on Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities, skills and knowledge to be developed, and career aspiration
Written confirmation of full-time enrolment from the relevant university and/or institution, or written confirmation of application and/or research proposal submitted
Current Curriculum Vitae (CV), a high-resolution corporate headshot in jpeg format, and a copy of the most up-to-date official academic transcript
Budget outlining how Scholarship funds will be used (downloadable template within the application form)
Confirmation of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander identity through a signed statement from an incorporated Indigenous organisation or Land Council

One written reference from an Elder or a senior member of your community, plus two written academic references OR one academic and one professional written reference; all references must be emailed by the referee directly to scholarships@aurorafoundation.com.au
selection_criteria: Ability to demonstrate how the study or research will impact Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities in improving cancer-related outcomes
Demonstrated aspiration towards employment or continued employment in a cancer-related field
Connection to, and contributions within, the Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander community (assessed through the personal statement and the Elder or senior community member reference)
Capability to undertake and complete the proposed full-time study or research (assessed through academic and/or professional references and the academic transcript)
coverage: Accommodation and/or travel expenses related to research, fieldwork or conferences
Textbooks and other essential study-related equipment, and computer hardware, software, and internet
Living expenses (for example, accommodation, transportation, food and other dietary requirements)
Access to academic, health and wellbeing services, and other academic and study-related resources
application_method: Read the First Nations Cancer Scholarship Guidelines (linked from Aurora's scholarship page) to confirm eligibility and required documents
Submit an application with all required documents via Aurora's Indigenous Pathways Portal before the closing date
Arrange for referees to email written references directly to scholarships@aurorafoundation.com.au
Optionally contact the Aurora Pathways Scholarship team at scholarships@aurorafoundation.com.au to discuss the application before applying
official.application_route: Online application through Aurora's Indigenous Pathways Portal; referees email references directly to the Scholarships team
official.citizenship_residency: Open to applicants of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander descent who identify as such and are accepted as such by their community; identity must be confirmed in writing by an incorporated Indigenous organisation or Land Council
official.international_eligibility: Eligibility is based on Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander identity rather than nationality; study or research may be undertaken at recognised universities or institutes in Australia, the US or the UK
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Full-time postgraduate study (graduate certificate, masters or PhD) or research in a cancer-related field in health, research or policy; the guidelines publish a list of applicable clinical and allied health, policy and research fields
official.research_requirement: Written confirmation of full-time enrolment in a postgraduate course, or written confirmation from a recognised research institute (or of an application/research proposal submitted); a budget for use of funds must be provided
official.duration: Up to three years (no need to re-apply each year once awarded)
official.description: Established by the Aurora Education Foundation and Cancer Australia and funded by the Australian Government through Cancer Australia, the First Nations Cancer Scholarship supports Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander graduate students, health professionals and early-career researchers to undertake full-time postgraduate study or research in a cancer-related field. Aurora frames the program as building the skills and knowledge required to improve cancer outcomes for Indigenous communities and increasing the number of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander leaders in cancer-related fields.
official.region: Oceania (study or research may be at recognised institutions in Australia, the US or the UK)
official.program_type: Scholarship program funded by the Australian Government through Cancer Australia, administered by the Aurora Education Foundation

not_confirmed: 2027 application window and deadline (not published as at the verification date)
individual or minimum award values (only the up-to $120,000 AUD per year cap is published)
verification.notes: Amount, coverage, eligibility, documents and 2026 cycle dates verified against Aurora's official scholarship page and Indigenous Pathways Portal listing; no English-language requirement is published on any official page.

applicant_utility.summary: One of Australia's largest Indigenous scholarships, worth up to $120,000 per year for up to three years plus up to $5,000 a year for tailored academic and wellbeing support, usable for university fees or HECS, living costs, equipment and conference travel - but only for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander applicants in full-time cancer-related postgraduate study or research. The 2026 round closed on 11 September 2026 and Aurora publishes awards 'yearly from 2024 to 2026', so treat any future window as unconfirmed until Aurora announces one. Because the file is document-heavy and Aurora states incomplete applications fail shortlisting, start collecting your identity confirmation, enrolment evidence and references months before a round opens.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander health professionals, graduate students and early-career researchers committed full-time to cancer-related study or research that benefits their own communities.
application_readiness_checklist: Request the signed identity confirmation from an incorporated Indigenous organisation or Land Council first - it is mandatory and can take weeks
Secure written confirmation of full-time enrolment (or of your submitted application/research proposal) from your university or research institute
Draft the two-page personal statement against Aurora's five required elements, including your community contribution and cancer-career aspiration
Ask your two referees (and the Elder or senior community member) early, and confirm they will email references directly to scholarships@aurorafoundation.com.au
Complete the budget template from the application form, disclosing all other funding and income
Prepare a high-resolution corporate headshot in jpeg and your latest official academic transcript
common_rejection_risks: Incomplete document sets: Aurora explicitly states applications missing required documents at closing will not be considered complete or pass shortlisting
Missing or unsigned Indigenous identity confirmation from an incorporated organisation or Land Council
References forwarded by the applicant instead of emailed directly by the referee
A course or project that cannot be clearly shown to be cancer-related in health, research or policy
Part-time enrolment, or no confirmation of enrolment or research-institute status
A budget that omits other income or funding sources
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Anything above the up-to-$120,000-per-year award value, plus any study or research expense Aurora states the university or institute should cover (the guidelines bar using funds for those). Relocation and personal costs not tied to research, fieldwork or conferences are not listed among eligible uses, so assume you fund those yourself.
document_audit: Identity confirmation must be a signed statement from an incorporated Indigenous organisation or Land Council - a personal declaration is not sufficient
The personal statement is capped at two pages and must cover five specific elements, including your connection to community and your cancer-field career aspiration
References only count when the referee emails them directly to scholarships@aurorafoundation.com.au
The budget must disclose all your additional funding and income, not just planned spending
The headshot must be a high-resolution jpeg, and the transcript must be your most recent official version
alerts: The 2026 round closed 11 September 2026; no 2027 window is published and Aurora describes awards running 'yearly from 2024 to 2026', so future rounds are not guaranteed
Only up to four scholarships are awarded each year across Australia, the US and the UK - expect a highly competitive field
Once awarded you do not re-apply each year, but the award is tied to full-time cancer-related study or research, so dropping below a full-time load puts it at risk
Study can be at recognised institutions in Australia, the US or the UK - confirm your institution's status with the Scholarships team before applying
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Submit the complete application through Aurora's Indigenous Pathways Portal before closing while referees email their references directly; Aurora shortlists only complete applications.
